title: Body-Reservoir Governance in Repeated Games: Embodied Decision-Making, Dynamic Sentinel Adaptation, and Complexity-Regularized Optimization
description:
Code, data, and manuscript for the paper Body-Reservoir Governance in Repeated Games.

We model game-theoretic agents as echo state networks (reservoir computers) and define the variational free energy of a strategy as prediction error plus complexity cost (KL divergence between driven and natural dynamics). A three-layer Body-Reservoir Governance (BRG) architecture — body (reservoir), cognitive filter, and metacognitive mixer — explains why unconditional cooperation can persist in practice despite Tit-for-Tat dominating in classical theory. Ten numerical experiments on a continuous Prisoner's Dilemma confirm all theoretical predictions using 20-seed Monte Carlo simulations with zero external dependencies.
